The 5 V line is fine with 26 AWG: the highest current is about 1 A, and 25 cm out and back only drops about 0.07 V. Jumper wires are usually 20 cm; the ones listed as 20 cm and up are tight, so extend with an M-F wire if short.

Why this way? Level 1 is only 30 mm tall, so it holds low items that are rarely touched: converters and power joints. The DevKit and the S3 board need height for upright jumper wires, so they go up to levels 2 and 3. The big breadboard is replaced by two 400-hole breadboards, one per board, so each board's wires are short.
Every item has a place, nothing touches the plate above it, the cells can be pulled out, and every cut wire reaches its end.
OK to lock in The position of every item on the three levels, after photographing. This is a gate: once it passes, the whole layout is considered final.

After it passes, mounting the level-1 items (Stage 2: the modules, not the wire connections not yet made) does not depend on Parts 3-5, so it can be done earlier as long as the top plate stays off. The servo power wire (Part 2 Stage 4) and the camera wire (Part 4 Stage 3) are connected to level 1 once made.

The display flickers or the S3 restarts when the speaker is loud: 5 V is dropping. Lower the volume, make sure LM2596 #1 is not supplying the camera, or fit a 470 µF capacitor on the S3 board's 5V pin.
The bot greets you but "badan belum terhubung": the DevKit is not getting 5 V (check the wire to the 30P power block) or a UART wire came off during assembly.
First test on the floor

Why this way? Ultrasonic sensors have a narrow field of view (about 15°) and do not see thin objects (chair legs) or soft objects. This robot is safe for a living room, but do not leave it driving alone near stairs: no sensor sees the floor disappearing.
The robot moves as commanded, stops by itself in front of an obstacle, and the STOP button always wins.

If something does not work
Most likely cause
Robot switches off by itself when the motors start
weak battery, or the BMS cuts out because of a current spike
charge the battery; check the fuse; lower the starting speed
ESP32 restarts randomly while the motors run
motor noise, poor GND
100 nF capacitor on each motor, 470 µF on VM, join the GNDs at a single point

motor wire came loose, or the TB6612 channel gets no signal

Caring for the battery and the robot
Switch off after use. The BMS still draws a small current; do not store it for weeks with the cells in the holders.
Charge the battery when the robot sends a low-battery warning (6.4 V total). Never let a cell drop below 3.0 V.
A cell that gets hot while charging, swells, or smells: stop, put it somewhere safe, and do not use it again.
Tighten the motor bolts and screw terminals from time to time; vibration loosens them.
Next ideas: wheel encoders (the code wheel from the chassis kit) for exact distance travelled, a line sensor to follow a path, or a cliff sensor under the front.
